test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 11 Oct 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
A wire is in the form of a square of side 33 cm. If the wire is molded to form a circle, then what is the radius of the circle? 

(Use pi = {22 over 7})
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a wire is remolded, the total length (perimeter) remains constant.

Circumference of Circle = Perimeter of Square

2 × (22 / 7) × r = 4 × 33

(44 / 7) × r = 132 ⇒ r = 3 × 7 = 21 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 21 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of the square (a) = 33 cm

π = 22 / 7

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of a square = 4 × a

Circumference of a circle = 2 × π × r (where r is the radius)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b90186e50b7eef4f799c922119a5273b552448e8dedb8f9f7e61429e76863ca4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total length of the wire = Perimeter of the square

⇒ Total length of the wire = 4 × 33 = 132 cm

⇒ When the same wire is bent into a circle, Circumference = Total length of the wire

⇒ 2 × π × r = 132

⇒ 2 × (22 / 7) × r = 132

⇒ (44 / 7) × r = 132

⇒ r = (132 × 7) ÷ 44

⇒ r = 3 × 7

⇒ r = 21 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 21 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Remolding 2D Shapes

When a wire is bent or reshaped from one 2D figure to another, its total length or boundary perimeter always remains constant.

Area and Perimeter Relation

For a given constant perimeter, a circle always encloses the maximum possible area compared to any other 2D polygon like a square, rectangle or triangle.

Remolding 3D Shapes

Similar to 2D figures, when a solid 3D object is melted and recast into another shape, its total volume remains strictly constant.
